messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT -> p99 latency SLO breached for /v1/stream generate (us-west-2). Triggered at 2026-03-15T12:34:00Z. Runbook: streaming-tail.

maria: seeing a hard p95/p99 spike starting ~12:33 UTC. p95 ~800ms -> baseline 120ms, p99 ~2.4s. Streaming responses showing stalls / partial frames. Dash: https://grafana.company/reports/streams/2489 (link) :alarm_clock:

sam: cache miss rate for prefix-cache jumped massively at the same time. prefix_cache_miss_rate went from ~4% -> 72% in 1m. looks like a prefix mismatch/invalidations flood. metric query: `sum(rate(prefix_cache_miss[1m])) by (shard)`

tia: we shipped prefix-hash tweak (prefixhash v2) in the 12:10 canary rollout — small change to canonicalization hashing to reduce collisions. rollout flag `use_prefixhash_v2=true` on ~10% of traffic.

alex: possible correlation. either the hash change produced new namespaces or TTL/namespace keys changed -> cold miss wave. Suggest immediate mitigation: toggle flag back on canary and enable routing fallback to older prefix variant.

sam: starting config flip now: `/featureflag set use_prefixhash_v2=false --scope=canary`

deploy-bot: Received request to set featureflag `use_prefixhash_v2=false` for canary. Starting toggle.

opsbot: Rollout toggle completed (canary). Verifying traffic shift.

maria: after toggle, I still see elevated misses for a few shards; p99 dipping but not fully recovered. p95 now ~240ms, p99 ~520ms (12:38).

sam: adding an emergency prefetch bump while the cache warms. patching prefetch workers + enabling async prefetch on streaming path. patch snippet: ```yaml
# one-off override for hot path
prefetch:
  workers: 6 -> 10
  async: true
  ttl_seconds: 900
```

alex: also enabling routing fallback to older model variants for streaming to reduce tail impact: `/routing set fallback_policy=legacy-prefix --routes=/v1/stream`

deploy-bot: Routing change applied to streaming route.

maria: quick sanity check logs from one affected node: ```
[12:33:12] cache: miss prefix='user:ENG-' -> computed-hash=0x7f3a
[12:33:12] loader: cache_miss -> fetching from KV backend (latency 180ms)
[12:33:14] stream: stall detected, waiting for kv (timeout 2.0s)
```

james-cs: customer-impact: two mid-market customers reported higher latencies and a small number of aborted streams. They've been notified and escalated to SE. SLO dashboard shows ~1.8% of requests breached p99 SLO window during the spike.

tia: root cause hypothesis: mismatch between prefix canonicalization in prefixhash-v2 and existing cached keys + aggressive cache TTL/rotation during rollout. cache invalidation storms + synchronous fetches caused downstream stalls.

sam: mitigation status: 1) featureflag rollback done on canary; 2) routing fallback enabled; 3) prefetch workers increased; 4) KV backend read parallelism raised on affected shards. Observed impacts: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~320ms by 12:42.

maria: continuing to monitor. preparing handoff notes for next oncall. please capture any remaining anomalies.

alex: next steps for postmortem: collect timeline of rollout, list of keys/namespace differences between hash versions, validate TTL/invalidation cadence, run a synthetic replay to reproduce cold-miss flood. Also recommend adding a canary traffic check that measures prefix_cache_miss_rate delta > 5% pre-future rollouts.

opsbot: Incident severity downgraded to S2. Moving to monitoring & handoff.

oncall-bot: Handing off to next oncall (sam -> alex) at 2026-03-15T12:50Z. Please follow runbook: streaming-tail -> postmortem-template.

alex: Handoff ack. I'll take owner for postmortem and follow up with infra to coordinate KV TTL tuning and a fix for canonicalization fallback.

maria: notes for postmortem: timeline, metrics (p95/p99 before, during, after), featureflag state changes, config patches, customer impact, mitigation commands used.

james-cs: CS will follow up with affected customers w/ timeline and mitigation summary.

-- END THREAD --
